correctness.rationale: The compatibility graph has the 128 binary words of length 7 as vertices, with an edge exactly when the two distinct deletion balls intersect in fewer than two outputs. A fresh independent reconstruction of all deletion balls verified that the 70 certificate codewords form a compatibility clique and that the supplied 70-color assignment is proper on all 7807 compatibility edges. Thus the witness gives a lower bound of 70 and the proper coloring gives a matching upper bound, proving the exact optimum and the stated redundancy.

value.rationale: The certificate resolves one exact coding parameter correctly, but the submitted package does not give a mathematical reason that blocklength 7 is a structural boundary, first unresolved case, transition point, or representative classification cutoff. It neither classifies optimal codes nor connects the value 70 to a general finite-length phenomenon. Under the common value standard, a single computationally tractable length chosen without such motivation is an arbitrary finite slice rather than an independently valuable exact invariant.
residual_risks: If length 7 is established elsewhere as the first previously unresolved finite case, that missing motivation would materially change the value assessment.

limitations: The rejection is for scientific value, not correctness or best-of-knowledge originality.
Only binary blocklength 7, one deletion and two distinct reads are resolved; no minimality, first-open-boundary claim or extremizer classification is supplied.
